purpose: Tracks, per G20+ expansion candidate, whether each required source-authority category has an official source identified and/or verified on file. This file records research state only. It never grants publication status — that happens exclusively through the existing data/rules/<slug>.json six-gate pipeline.

intake_status_model_notes.not_started: No candidate authority has been identified for this category yet.
intake_status_model_notes.identified: A plausible official authority name is known (public knowledge), but no specific official source URL has been fetched, dated, or cited yet.
intake_status_model_notes.needs_verification: A source URL exists from prior internal research but has not been re-checked for current reachability/effective text under this intake process.
intake_status_model_notes.verified_on_file: A specific official source URL is already recorded in the corresponding data/rules/<slug>.json source_authorities and was live-verified during that entry's own research (per the existing six-gate pipeline) — restated here for tracking only, not re-verified by this file.
intake_status_model_notes.not_applicable: This source category is not currently believed to be needed for this candidate's currency-passage rules (starting assumption only, may change once research begins).

not_applicable_note: tax_treasury_ministry_source is marked not_applicable for every candidate below because no candidate in this G20+ intake round has an identified currency-passage rule that depends specifically on a tax/treasury/ministry source distinct from its central bank or customs authority. This may change during actual research; not_applicable is a starting assumption, not a permanent exclusion.

customs_or_border_authority.label: US Customs and Border Protection (CBP) — Currency & Monetary Instrument Reporting
customs_or_border_authority.note: CBP is the administering border agency. Traveler currency-declaration requirement live-verified 2026-07-23 in primary law: 31 U.S.C. 5316 and 31 CFR 1010.340 (FinCEN Form 105 / CMIR) — a person transporting monetary instruments over USD 10,000 into or out of the US must file a report. This is a mandatory traveler border declaration, DISTINCT from institutional CTR/SAR/FBAR reporting. P8B-2 (2026-07-23): declaration now sourced to official eCFR 31 CFR 1010.340, official U.S. Code 31 U.S.C. 5316, and the official FinCEN Form 105 (CMIR) PDF (Cornell LII kept only as secondary mirror); off-topic CBP prohibited-items URL removed; CBP named in prose as administering agency. P8B-2b (2026-07-23, revised): current-account claims CLOSED via the IMF 2026 Article IV Consultation (CR 2026/076) — free-floating, Article VIII, no restrictions on current international payments, security exception; the generic IMF country-page citation was removed. Capital-account/account-access fields (resident, non-resident, banking) RETAIN [HARDENING] — OECD Code Annex B US reservation record not extractable with available tooling. publish_ready blocked; US held at source_review_ready.

financial_intelligence_unit_or_aml_autho.label: Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) — BSA Reporting Requirements
financial_intelligence_unit_or_aml_autho.note: FinCEN homepage live-verified 2026-07-23 (fincen.gov) — Treasury BSA administrator, but generic; it does not itself document Form 105/CMIR. The traveler declaration rests on the customs cross-border transport report (Form 105/CMIR under 31 USC 5316 / 31 CFR 1010.340), NOT on FinCEN's institutional CTR (31 USC 5313) / SAR / FBAR regime — do not conflate. Resolved in P8B-2 (2026-07-23): re-tagged to type 'fiu' in data/rules/united-states.json, and the declaration is sourced to 31 CFR 1010.340 / 31 U.S.C. 5316 (FinCEN Form 105 / CMIR).

central_bank_or_monetary_authority.label: South African Reserve Bank (SARB), Financial Surveillance Department — exchange control
central_bank_or_monetary_authority.note: P8C-1 live-verified 2026-07-23: FinSurv Documents page (resbank.co.za/en/home/what-we-do/financial-surveillance/financial-surveillance-documents) and the controlling Currency and Exchanges Manual for Authorised Dealers, version 2026-05-15, plus 2026 exchange-control circulars. Governs exchange-control approvals, authorised-dealer rules, and the R25,000 rand / R100,000 excess-currency limits — DISTINCT from the SARS customs declaration and from FIC AML reporting. The generic resbank.co.za homepage in data/rules/south-africa.json should be replaced with these claim-specific URLs in the publication-candidate review.

customs_or_border_authority.label: South African Revenue Service (SARS) — customs traveller currency declaration
customs_or_border_authority.note: P8C-1 live-verified 2026-07-23: SARS Travellers page (sars.gov.za/customs-and-excise/travellers/) — mandatory online Traveller Declaration for all travellers from 1 July 2026, plus manual TD-01; excess currency exceeding R100,000 (or foreign currency convertible to Rand over R100,000) requires SARB written permission. SARS administers the customs declaration; SARB governs exchange control — do not conflate. Generic sars.gov.za homepage in data/rules should be replaced with claim-specific URLs in the publication-candidate review.
